blocks.raw: # API lifecycle
blocks.text: API lifecycle

blocks.raw: This guide explains how DriveWealth manages the lifecycle of its APIs — from early availability through general release to eventual deprecation. Understanding these stages helps you build integrations that are stable, forward-compatible, and easy to maintain.
blocks.text: This guide explains how DriveWealth manages the lifecycle of its APIs — from early availability through general release to eventual deprecation. Understanding these stages helps you build integrations that are stable, forward-compatible, and easy to maintain.

blocks.raw: ## **Lifecycle stages**
blocks.text: Lifecycle stages
Beta

blocks.raw: A **Beta** endpoint is available in the UAT (sandbox) environment for integration testing. Beta endpoints are not available in production.
blocks.text: A Beta endpoint is available in the UAT (sandbox) environment for integration testing. Beta endpoints are not available in production.

blocks.raw: A beta endpoint is identified by the `beta` tag in the API reference.
blocks.text: A beta endpoint is identified by the beta tag in the API reference.

blocks.raw: **What to expect during beta:**
blocks.text: What to expect during beta:

blocks.raw:
* The endpoint is functional and testable in UAT
* Request and response schemas may change before GA
* There is no committed timeline for GA promotion
blocks.text: The endpoint is functional and testable in UATRequest and response schemas may change before GAThere is no committed timeline for GA promotion

blocks.raw: **Recommendations:**
blocks.text: Recommendations:

blocks.raw:
* Do not release beta-dependent features to end customers in production
* Monitor the <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://developer.drivewealth.com/apis/changelog">changelog</Anchor> for updates to beta endpoints
* Treat any schema changes during beta as expected, not breaking
blocks.text: Do not release beta-dependent features to end customers in productionMonitor the changelog for updates to beta endpointsTreat any schema changes during beta as expected, not breaking

blocks.raw: ### **General Availability (GA)**
blocks.text: General Availability (GA)

blocks.raw: A **GA** endpoint has had its `beta` tag removed and is available in both UAT and production environments.
blocks.text: A GA endpoint has had its beta tag removed and is available in both UAT and production environments.

blocks.raw: GA endpoints are covered by DriveWealth's API stability guarantees. Any breaking changes to a GA endpoint will follow the deprecation process described below.
blocks.text: GA endpoints are covered by DriveWealth's API stability guarantees. Any breaking changes to a GA endpoint will follow the deprecation process described below.

blocks.raw: **What you can rely on with GA endpoints:**
blocks.text: What you can rely on with GA endpoints:

blocks.raw:
* The endpoint is stable and production-ready
* Schema changes will be additive and non-breaking (see [Breaking vs. non-breaking changes](#breaking-vs-non-breaking-changes))
* Advance notice will be given before any breaking changes
* The endpoint appears in the changelog when it graduates from beta
blocks.text: The endpoint is stable and production-readySchema changes will be additive and non-breaking (see Breaking vs. non-breaking changes)Advance notice will be given before any breaking changesThe endpoint appears in the changelog when it graduates from beta

blocks.raw: ### **Deprecated**
blocks.text: Deprecated

blocks.raw: A **Deprecated** endpoint is marked with a `deprecated` tag in the API reference. It remains available in both UAT and production but should not be used for new integrations.
blocks.text: A Deprecated endpoint is marked with a deprecated tag in the API reference. It remains available in both UAT and production but should not be used for new integrations.

blocks.raw: Deprecated endpoints have a defined sunset date after which they will be removed entirely.
blocks.text: Deprecated endpoints have a defined sunset date after which they will be removed entirely.

blocks.raw: **What to expect when an endpoint is deprecated:**
blocks.text: What to expect when an endpoint is deprecated:

blocks.raw:
* A deprecation notice is published in the <Anchor target="_blank" href="https://developer.drivewealth.com/apis/changelog">changelog</Anchor>
* The sunset date is stated in the deprecation notice — typically a minimum of **12 months** from the deprecation date
* The endpoint continues to function until the sunset date
* DriveWealth will communicate migration guidance alongside the deprecation notice
blocks.text: A deprecation notice is published in the changelogThe sunset date is stated in the deprecation notice — typically a minimum of 12 months from the deprecation dateThe endpoint continues to function until the sunset dateDriveWealth will communicate migration guidance alongside the deprecation notice

blocks.raw: **Recommendations:**
blocks.text: Recommendations:

blocks.raw:
* Begin planning your migration as soon as you see a deprecation notice
* Do not build new features on deprecated endpoints
* Contact your DriveWealth integration manager if the timeline creates a problem for your roadmap
blocks.text: Begin planning your migration as soon as you see a deprecation noticeDo not build new features on deprecated endpointsContact your DriveWealth integration manager if the timeline creates a problem for your roadmap

blocks.raw: ### **Retired**
blocks.text: Retired

blocks.raw: A **retired** endpoint has been fully removed. Requests to a sunset endpoint will return a `410 Gone` response.
blocks.text: A retired endpoint has been fully removed. Requests to a sunset endpoint will return a 410 Gone response.

blocks.raw: ## **Lifecycle at a glance**
blocks.text: Lifecycle at a glance

blocks.raw:
| Stage          | UAT | Production | Stability guarantee | Action required           |
| :------------- | :-- | :--------- | :------------------ | :------------------------ |
| **Beta**       | ✅   | ❌          | None                | Test and provide feedback |
| **GA**         | ✅   | ✅          | ✅                   | Build against             |
| **Deprecated** | ✅   | ✅          | Until sunset date   | Plan migration            |
| **Retired**    | ❌   | ❌          | —                   | Migrate immediately       |

blocks.raw: ## **Breaking vs. non-breaking changes**
blocks.text: Breaking vs. non-breaking changes

blocks.raw: DriveWealth distinguishes between changes that require action on your part and changes that are safe to absorb automatically.
blocks.text: DriveWealth distinguishes between changes that require action on your part and changes that are safe to absorb automatically.

blocks.raw: ### **Breaking changes**
blocks.text: Breaking changes

blocks.raw: A breaking change is any modification that can cause an existing, correctly-written integration to fail or behave incorrectly without code changes on your side.
blocks.text: A breaking change is any modification that can cause an existing, correctly-written integration to fail or behave incorrectly without code changes on your side.

blocks.raw: DriveWealth will **never** introduce breaking changes to a GA endpoint without first deprecating it and providing a migration path.
blocks.text: DriveWealth will never introduce breaking changes to a GA endpoint without first deprecating it and providing a migration path.

blocks.raw: Breaking changes include:
blocks.text: Breaking changes include:

blocks.raw:
* Removing an endpoint entirely
* Removing a required or optional request field
* Removing a response field
* Renaming a field
* Changing a field's data type (e.g. `string` → `integer`)
* Changing a field's format in a meaningful way (e.g. date format `YYYY-MM-DD` → Unix timestamp)
* Changing an HTTP method (e.g. `POST` → `PUT`)
* Changing a URL path or path parameter
* Adding a new **required** request field
* Changing authentication requirements
* Narrowing the range of accepted values for a field (e.g. reducing the max length of a string)
* Removing or renaming an enum value that appears in responses

blocks.raw: ### **Non-breaking changes**
blocks.text: Non-breaking changes

blocks.raw: A non-breaking change can be introduced to GA endpoints at any time without a deprecation cycle. Well-written integrations should absorb these changes gracefully.
blocks.text: A non-breaking change can be introduced to GA endpoints at any time without a deprecation cycle. Well-written integrations should absorb these changes gracefully.

blocks.raw: Non-breaking changes include:
blocks.text: Non-breaking changes include:

blocks.raw:
* Adding a new optional request field
* Adding a new response field
* Adding a new endpoint
* Adding a new enum value to a **request** field (see note below)
* Relaxing validation (e.g. increasing the max length of a string)
* Changing the order of fields in a JSON response
* Adding new error codes to the documented error set
* Performance improvements with no observable behavior change
blocks.text: Adding a new optional request fieldAdding a new response fieldAdding a new endpointAdding a new enum value to a request field (see note below)Relaxing validation (e.g. increasing the max length of a string)Changing the order of fields in a JSON responseAdding new error codes to the documented error setPerformance improvements with no observable behavior change

blocks.raw: **Note on new enum values in responses:** If your integration deserializes responses into a strict enum type, a new response enum value can cause a runtime error. DriveWealth recommends using permissive deserialization for enum fields and treating unknown values as a signal to check the changelog — not as a hard failure.
blocks.text: Note on new enum values in responses: If your integration deserializes responses into a strict enum type, a new response enum value can cause a runtime error. DriveWealth recommends using permissive deserialization for enum fields and treating unknown values as a signal to check the changelog — not as a hard failure.

blocks.raw: ### **How to write a resilient integration**
blocks.text: How to write a resilient integration

blocks.raw: Following these practices will ensure your integration handles non-breaking changes without requiring code changes:
blocks.text: Following these practices will ensure your integration handles non-breaking changes without requiring code changes:

blocks.raw:
* **Ignore unknown fields.** Do not reject responses that contain fields your code does not recognize.
* **Use permissive enum handling.** Log and skip unknown enum values rather than throwing an error.
* **Do not rely on field ordering.** JSON object field order is not guaranteed.
* **Check for **`null`** explicitly.** Do not assume that a field present today will always have a non-null value.
